skim: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak becomes its deadliest on record with 2,325 deaths, as Zambia’s Hichilema claims a contested second term and Colombia shifts from earthquake rescue to recovery with the toll at 289.
Trump threatened to ‘bomb’ Oman if it ‘gets in the way’ of a Hormuz deal as the US-Iran deadline expired, while Kushner and Netanyahu agreed a US general should oversee Hamas’s disarmament.
Nvidia guaranteed up to $105 billion for OpenAI’s new Ohio data-centre lease as the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in nearly 20 years and Stripe closed its $7bn-plus OpenRouter buy.
Reform UK unveiled a $68bn welfare-cut blueprint targeting foreign nationals and PIP claimants, as Jharkhand students set an Aug 20 deadline to gherao Chief Minister Soren’s residence.
Rodri sealed a £65m switch to Barcelona from Manchester City as India took a 178-run lead over Sri Lanka at Galle, with F1 returning to Zandvoort for Verstappen’s home-track farewell.

stories.headline: DR Congo’s Ebola Outbreak Becomes Deadliest on Record
stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the country’s deadliest ever, with 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed cases — a 46% fatality rate that has now surpassed the previous record of 2,299 deaths set in 2018-2020, per UN News (Aug 17). The WHO warned the outbreak is “outpacing the response,” saying “responders need safe access to communities, and the resources to end this outbreak and save lives,” as it launches a major scale-up backed by a $54.5 million OCHA allocation and vaccine trials now underway in the UK and Canada.

stories.headline: Zambia’s Hichilema Wins Second Term Amid Fraud Allegations
stories.body: Zambia’s electoral commission declared President Hakainde Hichilema the winner of a second term with roughly 60% of the vote to challenger Brian Mundubile’s 38%, per Al Jazeera (Aug 18). The count that resumed after Sunday’s violence and ballot theft remained contested, with police arresting 11 people — including opposition figures — in a raid involving gunfire, while Mundubile alleged manipulation of results forms and demanded an independent investigation that Hichilema’s campaign dismissed as false.

stories.headline: Colombia Shifts From Rescue to Recovery as Earthquake Toll Hits 289
stories.body: Colombia’s death toll from the magnitude-7.4 earthquake rose to at least 289, with 143 people officially unaccounted for, as authorities began winding down search-and-rescue in favour of reconstruction, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). “Certain search-and-rescue operations are no longer necessary, and we have now moved on to a phase in which reconstruction, demolition, and other types of operations… will begin,” said Sergeant Joel Bustamante, as officials work to house more than 120,000 affected families, many now sheltering in converted stadiums and community centres.

stories.headline: Indonesia Quake Toll Climbs to 68 as Survivors Report No Government Aid
stories.body: The death toll from Indonesia’s magnitude-7.7 Flores earthquake rose to 68, with more than 200 injured and roughly 12,800 people still displaced, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). “Our houses are no longer liveable because many have collapsed and are full of cracks,” said survivor Junaidin, adding “as for help from the government, there hasn’t been any — no tents, no medicine, no food,” even as the military airlifted 13 tonnes of emergency supplies to the island.

stories.headline: Suthar-Jadeja Spin Web Hands India 178-Run Lead at Galle
stories.body: India were bowled out for 462 on the third morning at Galle — Devdutt Padikkal’s maiden Test century (167), KL Rahul’s 82 and Dhruv Jurel’s 51 built the total — before Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja shared seven wickets to dismiss Sri Lanka for 284, per ESPNcricinfo (Aug 17). Sonal Dinusha made a maiden century and Niroshan Dickwella added 80 in a defiant middle-order stand, but India closed day three 178 runs ahead with two days left and rain still threatening the Test, per Outlook India (Aug 17).

stories.headline: Rodri Completes £65m Move to Barcelona From Man City
stories.body: Manchester City have accepted Barcelona’s bid of roughly £65.4m ($88.5m) for Rodri, with the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner signing a four-year deal after seven seasons and 298 appearances in Manchester, per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). The 30-year-old World Cup winner won 12 major honours at City — including four Premier League titles and the Champions League — and now joins Barcelona’s midfield after Frenkie de Jong’s expected lengthy injury lay-off helped open the door for the move.

stories.headline: Zandvoort’s Farewell: Verstappen Chases History Amid Winless Run
stories.body: Formula 1 resumes after its summer break at Zandvoort for what organisers confirm is the circuit’s final race on the calendar, with Max Verstappen chasing a fourth home win to match Jim Clark’s record and end a winless run stretching back to June, per GPblog (Aug 17). “I just want to enjoy it with the fans,” Verstappen said of the farewell weekend, as Honda debuts an upgraded power unit tested during the summer break at Aston Martin’s Hungaroria filming day.

stories.headline: Salah Makes Trabzonspor Debut After Shock Liverpool Exit
stories.body: Mohamed Salah made his full debut for Trabzonspor as a 58th-minute substitute in a 1-1 draw at Kasimpasa, days after completing a free transfer from Liverpool that ended his eight-year spell at Anfield, per beIN Sports (Aug 15). The 34-year-old fired his best chance over the crossbar in the 70th minute as Noah Saviolo’s opener for Trabzonspor was cancelled out by an Adrian Benedyczak penalty, marking one of the transfer window’s biggest surprises.

stories.headline: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Level in Nearly 20 Years
stories.body: The 30-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level in almost two decades — last seen around 2006, “when there was no iPhone and Lehman Brothers was a Wall Street titan” — as bond markets price in persistent deficits, inflation risk and long-term uncertainty, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 17). “Growth is cooling, the consumer is pulling back, and the bond market wants more money to wait,” the report noted, with the sell-off compounded by crude near $83 and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve sitting at 43-year lows.

stories.headline: China’s July Data Misses Across the Board as Stimulus Fades
stories.body: China’s industrial output grew just 4.5% year-on-year in July, down from 5.3% in June and below the 4.8% forecast, while retail sales rose only 0.6% — far short of the 1.5% expected — per Reuters via Investing.com (Aug 17). Fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% over the first seven months versus a forecast 6.0% drop, with Citi analysts noting subsidy-linked daily sales dropped to 6.3 billion yuan ($934.8 million) in July from 9 billion in June, as three typhoons and a tenth straight month of falling auto sales added to the drag.

stories.headline: VIX Hits 2026 Low Just as Strategists Warn of Seasonal Sell-Off Risk
stories.body: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) fell to 14.2 last Friday, its lowest reading since 2026 began, even as Wall Street sits at record highs, per BigGo Finance (Aug 17). “We are entering a window that has historically been prone to downside volatility, and we are doing so with the market at record highs and the VIX at year-to-date lows,” said BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky, while IG’s Axel Rudolph added “the market is starting to look a little too comfortable” — strategists point to a pattern since 1990 of at least a 7% equal-weight S&P 500 pullback between mid-August and mid-October in midterm election years.

stories.headline: Walmart, Target, Home Depot and Lowe’s Earnings This Week to Test Consumer Resilience
stories.body: Four major retailers — Walmart and Target (both Q2) plus Home Depot and Lowe’s — report earnings this week, arriving right after Americans “unexpectedly pulled back on retail spending in July by the biggest amount in more than a year,” per Fortune (Aug 17). The reports land with the S&P 500 near record highs and retailers grappling with “stubbornly high inflation and customers that are laser focused on prices,” making the results a direct read on whether the consumer-fatigue signal from last week’s retail sales report is broadening.

stories.headline: Gold Extends Rally to $4,440 as Weak Data Keeps Fed Hike Odds Fading
stories.body: Spot gold opened at $4,440.10/oz Monday, up 2.4% on the week and 32.7% year-over-year, after July retail sales fell 0.6% — far worse than the 0.1% gain economists expected — and August consumer sentiment slid 8%, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 17). Softer data continues to erode the odds of a September Fed rate hike and a weaker dollar (the Dollar Index dipped 0.2%) added further support, even as lingering Middle East tensions keep an inflation risk in the background.

stories.headline: Nvidia Guarantees Up to $105 Billion for OpenAI’s Ohio Data Center
stories.body: Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion in lease obligations for OpenAI’s planned 8-gigawatt AI campus in Pike County, Ohio — built on the site of a former Cold War uranium-enrichment plant — with capacity coming online in phases from 2028, per Unite.AI and Bloomberg (Aug 17). Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said “AI is becoming infrastructure — the foundation for intelligence in every industry — and land, power and shell have become vital in the age of AI,” with Nvidia on the hook to cover any shortfall if OpenAI defaults, deepening the circular financing ties binding the two companies; Nvidia is separately investing $1.5 billion in the project’s developer, SB Energy.

stories.headline: Stripe Finalizes $7 Billion-Plus OpenRouter Acquisition
stories.body: Stripe closed its purchase of AI model-routing startup OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, confirming last week’s reported talks, per Dataconomy (Aug 17). OpenRouter, which lets developers tap over 400 AI models through one gateway to avoid vendor lock-in, serves 8 million users and had raised its Series B at just a $1.3 billion valuation in May — a more than five-fold markup in three months; OpenRouter’s CEO has described the platform as “the equivalent of Stripe for AI.”

stories.headline: Amodei Defends His AI Messaging, Anthropic Details Claude Watermarking
stories.body: A day after calling the AI backlash a “crisis of trust,” Dario Amodei pushed back on investor Gavin Baker’s claim that his own risk warnings fueled anti-AI sentiment, arguing distrust stems from “a broader, long-standing crisis of trust in corporations and government” rather than AI executives’ warnings, while conceding the “most legitimate criticism” of firms like Anthropic is their failure to deliver tangible benefits so far, per The AI Insider (Aug 17). Anthropic also published details of a new Claude text-watermarking system built for EU AI Act compliance, using subtle, SynthID-Text-style word-choice patterns “undetectable to readers without a decoding key” that survive light editing but not full rewrites.

stories.headline: Meta’s $420 Billion in Off-Balance-Sheet AI Debt Draws Scrutiny
stories.body: Days after Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto met public skepticism, a Wall Street Journal analysis found Meta carries roughly $420 billion in off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments — nearly five times its reported $83.7 billion in debt — including $347 billion in future lease obligations and a Blue Owl Capital-backed joint venture financing its Hyperion data center that Ernst & Young flagged as a “critical audit matter,” per Tech Times (Aug 17). Meta’s free cash flow collapsed 91% to $784 million in Q2 despite strong revenue growth, prompting former Facebook investor Roger McNamee to call the spending spree “manufacturing appearance” rather than substance.

stories.headline: Fourth Woman Sues xAI Over Grok-Generated Child Abuse Images
stories.body: A Wyoming woman, identified as Jane Doe 4, joined an expanding lawsuit against xAI alleging her stepfather used Grok’s “Imagine” feature to turn a childhood photo of her into explicit images; he died by suicide two days after investigators found the images, per Engadget (Aug 17). She joins three Tennessee teenagers already suing over Grok-generated sexualized deepfakes distributed on Discord and Telegram, in a case that could cover “at least thousands of minors,” as California’s attorney general and EU regulators separately investigate X over AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens to ‘Bomb’ Oman as US-Iran Hormuz Deadline Expires
stories.body: The 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding on reopening the Strait of Hormuz expired Monday without a deal, prompting President Trump to warn on Fox News, “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb them,” per The Jerusalem Post (Aug 17). Trump also confirmed a direct US backchannel to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps and said he is in no rush for a deal, even as Iran’s foreign ministry said Tehran and Oman had reached “an understanding” on a Hormuz transit map letting ships pass near Iran and exit near Oman fee-free during an interim period, per The Times of Israel (Aug 17).

stories.headline: Kushner and Netanyahu Agree US General Should Oversee Hamas Disarmament
stories.body: A day after his rare direct Cairo talks with Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya, Jared Kushner met Netanyahu in Jerusalem, and an Israeli official said the two agreed “no redeployment or reconstruction would take place in the Gaza Strip before Hamas is disarmed,” with the first step requiring Hamas to “hand over its weapons for decommissioning under the supervision of an American general,” per Courthouse News Service (Aug 17). Analysts read the Hamas outreach as a shift in Washington’s posture — scholar Adel Shadid said “Hamas is no longer the problem in the American reading, but rather part of the solution,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 17) — even as Netanyahu, facing an Oct 27 election, keeps publicly rejecting elements of Trump’s 15-point roadmap.

stories.headline: UNIFIL: Lebanese Civilians ‘Paying the Highest Price’ as Israeli Strikes Intensify
stories.body: UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL said Israeli forces fired an average of 137 projectiles a day into Lebanon between Aug 5-16 — peaking at 208 on Saturday and 185 on Sunday — despite the June 26 ceasefire, warning that “civilians are once again paying the highest price, with many families displaced or forced to change their daily routines because of insecurity and uncertainty,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 17). The death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon since March 2 has reached 4,346, including 11 people killed in two separate air raids on Saturday alone.

stories.headline: Venezuela Frees Nearly 80 More Political Prisoners, Some Reporting Torture
stories.body: Venezuela’s transitional government released close to 80 more political prisoners on Aug 17, days after an initial batch of 131, per Local10/AP (Aug 17). Among them was Emirlendris Benitez, freed after eight years’ detention over an alleged 2018 drone attack on Nicolás Maduro, who says she was beaten and suffocated in custody and now uses a wheelchair from untreated medical complications; her mother said Benitez “wouldn’t hurt a fly.” Many newly freed prisoners still face restrictions, such as periodic court appearances, rather than full freedom, as the reconciliation process continues.

stories.headline: Sudan’s Army Downs Second RSF Drone This Month as Kordofan Fighting Rages
stories.body: Sudan’s military said it shot down an RSF-operated FH-95 drone over Gereikh in North Kordofan state on Aug 17 — the second advanced drone its air defences have downed in the region this month — per Sudan Tribune (Aug 17). The clash follows a late-July army offensive that reclaimed large swathes of North Kordofan, including a key export route, pushing the RSF westward and helping secure El Obeid and a land corridor to Omdurman.

fixtures.headline: 2nd Test Shifts to Colombo
fixtures.body: With the rain-hit Galle Test finishing Aug 19, India and Sri Lanka move to the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo for the series-deciding 2nd Test.

fixtures.headline: Premier League Kicks Off, Isak Returns to St James’ Park
fixtures.body: The 2026/27 Premier League season opens with Newcastle hosting Liverpool — Alexander Isak’s first return since forcing his move away — while Arsenal begin the title defence at home to Coventry City.

fixtures.headline: F1 Returns for Zandvoort’s Final Sprint Weekend
fixtures.body: Formula 1 restarts after the summer break with a sprint weekend at Zandvoort — practice and sprint qualifying Friday, sprint race and qualifying Saturday, and the Grand Prix Sunday — in what is set to be the circuit’s last appearance on the calendar.

fixtures.headline: Champions League League-Phase Draw
fixtures.body: UEFA holds the 2026/27 Champions League league-phase draw once the final qualifying rounds wrap up, setting the fixture list for Europe’s top clubs.

fixtures.headline: Duleep Trophy Begins
fixtures.body: India’s first-class season resumes with the Duleep Trophy’s zonal squads — Ruturaj Gaikwad captaining West Zone — serving as a proving ground for the next wave of Test contenders, with both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli sitting out.

portfolio.headline: Meta Faces Up to $1.4 Trillion in Potential Damages as California Child-Safety Trial Opens
portfolio.body: A trial brought by 29 state attorneys general opened in California, alleging Meta illegally collected children’s data and designed addictive product features, with potential damages cited in a range of $200 billion to $1.4 trillion; the case follows a New Mexico verdict that already ordered Meta to pay $942 million combined. Wall Street trimmed price targets on the stock as the trial began — UBS to $715, Baird to $750 and Goldman Sachs to $725 — though the consensus rating held at Buy. Per Benzinga (Aug 17).

portfolio.headline: Morgan Stanley Warns Hyperscaler AI Spending Is Outrunning Revenue
portfolio.body: Morgan Stanley flagged that the gap between AI capital spending and the revenue it generates is pressuring near-term cash flow across the hyperscalers, projecting industry capital spending will rise 57% in 2026 versus 2025 and warning some companies may need to raise additional debt at higher rates to bridge the gap. Microsoft, which has outlined roughly $190 billion of AI infrastructure investment, was named among the group under scrutiny, though the report noted the company holds $77 billion in cash against $129 billion in debt and is expected to generate about $67 billion in free cash flow this year. Per Yahoo Finance/The Motley Fool (Aug 17).

portfolio.headline: Oracle’s AI Backlog Swells to $638 Billion, but Investors Want Proof It Converts to Revenue
portfolio.body: Oracle disclosed that its remaining performance obligations — future contracted revenue including commitments from clients such as OpenAI and Meta — surged to $638 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter, up 363% year over year. Analysts said the market is assigning little valuation premium to that backlog until it converts into booked revenue, with JPMorgan maintaining an Overweight rating and a $200 price target; the disclosure landed in the same week Morgan Stanley questioned whether hyperscalers’ AI spending is outrunning their cash generation. Per TradingKey (Aug 16).

portfolio.headline: Twilio Gives Back Part of Its Post-Earnings Rally as the Software Trade Cools
portfolio.body: No new company-specific announcement was found for the session; Twilio’s pullback came a week and a half after it beat Q2 estimates and raised 2026 guidance alongside a completed $1.2 billion buyback. The retreat tracked a broader cooling in richly valued software names, following both the hyperscaler AI-financing warnings that hit Microsoft and Oracle and a step back from the M&A-driven software rally sparked by Silver Lake’s reported $51 billion approach for Workday. Per TheStreet (Aug 17).

portfolio.headline: Boeing Deliveries Lose Momentum Against Airbus as Regulators Order New 737 Max Inspections
portfolio.body: Boeing delivered 53 aircraft in July, down from 60-64 a month in the prior two months and behind Airbus’s 67, leaving Boeing at 367 deliveries year-to-date versus Airbus’s 418; the company did register 38 new orders in the month, including from AerCap, Luxair and Uganda National Airlines at the Farnborough Airshow. The delivery slowdown compounds an FAA directive requiring crack inspections on 471 737 Max jets after reports of a structural bear-strap issue on older Next-Generation 737s, with the rule taking effect September 10. Per AeroTime (Aug 12) and ABC News (Aug 7).

portfolio.headline: Rackspace’s Losses Deepen Even as Revenue Holds Steady
portfolio.body: Rackspace Technology reported Q2 2026 revenue of $670.1 million, essentially flat year over year, but its net loss widened to $67.5 million from $54.5 million a year earlier, with non-GAAP gross margin slipping to 18.6% from 19.8%. The company swung from a profitable first quarter into a loss-making second quarter, underscoring pressure on profitability even as its AI infrastructure pivot continues. Per Simply Wall St (Aug 12).

portfolio.headline: Beyond Meat Completes 1-for-30 Reverse Split to Save Its Nasdaq Listing
portfolio.body: Beyond Meat’s 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect at the close of trading on August 13, consolidating every 30 shares into one and cutting authorized common stock from 3 billion to 100 million shares, with convertible notes, warrants and award prices adjusted proportionately. The company said the move was intended to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s $1.00 minimum bid price rule ahead of an August 31 deadline. Per GlobeNewswire (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: Fortress Biotech Grows Revenue 14% and Boosts Cash Pile via Crystalys Financing
portfolio.body: Fortress Biotech reported Q2 2026 revenue of $18.7 million, up 14% from $16.4 million a year earlier and driven mainly by Journey Medical’s dermatology sales of $17.8 million, though it posted a net loss of $2.5 million versus net income in the prior-year quarter. Cash climbed to $196.6 million from $79.4 million at year-end after subsidiary Crystalys secured $130 million in Series B financing, while partner AstraZeneca reported a 62% improvement in survival in a subgroup analysis of anselamimab for cardiac amyloidosis. Per StockTitan (Aug 13).

portfolio.headline: Hydrofarm’s Q2 Revenue Nearly Halves as Oversupply and Brand Exits Bite
portfolio.body: Hydrofarm Holdings reported Q2 2026 revenue of $23.2 million, down 40.9% from $39.2 million a year earlier and well short of consensus, which the company attributed to industry oversupply and the discontinuation of certain distributed brands; adjusted loss per share also missed estimates. Gross margin nonetheless improved to 20.0% from 19.2%, and the company applied proceeds from the $16 million sale of its Aurora Peat Products unit, completed July 31, toward debt reduction. Per Investing.com (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Jharkhand Students Set Aug 18 Ultimatum Ahead of Aug 20 Gherao of CM Soren’s Residence
stories.body: On the 22nd day of their agitation, JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch leaders gave Chief Minister Hemant Soren an Aug 18 deadline to act on alleged exam-paper irregularities, warning that “lakhs of students and youths” would march on his Ranchi residence on Aug 20 if he does not comply, per Organiser (Aug 17). Soren used his Independence Day speech to promise an impartial probe and tech-secured exams, but protest leader Ravindra Paswan said the CM must resign unless a CBI or judicial probe, cancellation of the JSSC-CGL and JPSC results, and reinstatement of whistleblower Santosh Kumar Mastana are delivered.

stories.headline: Chamoli Tunnel Search Enters Fourth Day as Toll Holds at 8, Two Still Missing
stories.body: Rescue teams from the NDRF, SDRF and ITBP kept pumping water from the flooded THDC tunnel at Pipalkoti for a fourth straight day, still searching for Jharkhand’s Lucas Topno and Chhattisgarh’s Chetan Poyam after the Aug 13 landslide, with the death toll steady at eight and twelve workers already hospitalised, per The Hitavada (Aug 17). A magisterial inquiry ordered into the disaster’s cause remains ongoing as authorities have yet to reach the two men still trapped.

stories.headline: IMD Warns of Heavy Rain Sweeping North India Through Aug 22, Delhi Braces for Aug 18 Downpour
stories.body: The India Meteorological Department extended its heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall warning through Aug 22 as a Bay of Bengal low deepens into a depression, with Odisha, Gangetic West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand hit hardest on Aug 16–17 and the wet spell expanding to Delhi-NCR, Haryana and Punjab from Aug 18, per Business Today (Aug 17). Flash-flood and waterlogging risk is flagged for Odisha districts including Angul, Bargarh and Cuttack, with West Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand staying vulnerable through the outlook period.

stories.headline: Reform UK Details $68bn Welfare Cuts, Targeting Foreign Nationals and PIP
stories.body: Reform UK published its blueprint to strip roughly $68 billion a year from Britain’s welfare bill, split between about $28.5bn saved by ending universal credit, housing and disability payments for foreign nationals — including EU citizens with settled status — and $29.8bn from scrapping PIP for a more restrictive disability payment, per UPI (Aug 17). Work-and-pensions spokesman Danny Kruger said he would understand “if the Europeans decided to apply the same principle… to deny our nationals access to their welfare system,” while Labour MP Rachael Maskell warned the disability cuts would stop people playing “a full role in our society.”

stories.headline: Stourbridge Wildfire Investigation Under Way as Daily Briefings Continue for Residents
stories.body: Four days after wildfires destroyed 19 homes and damaged 18 more across roughly 500 acres of Stourbridge, investigators are still working to establish a cause while Dudley Council runs daily 2pm briefings — online and in person at the town hall — to update affected residents, per Birmingham Dispatch (Aug 17) and Express & Star (Aug 15). Councillor Ed Lawrence said the sessions give residents “a dedicated opportunity… to hear the latest updates and ask questions,” as the Prime Minister visited the town to thank fire crews and pledge recovery support.

stories.headline: Qatar’s Amir Discusses Bilateral Ties in Call With Bahrain’s King
stories.body: Qatar’s Amir received a phone call from the King of Bahrain, with the two leaders discussing “fraternal relations between the two countries and ways to support and strengthen them in various fields,” alongside regional and international issues of shared concern, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 17).

stories.headline: Qatar’s PM Pushes Hormuz De-escalation in Calls With Saudi, Jordanian, Syrian Counterparts
stories.body: Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani held back-to-back calls with the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Syria, stressing “the importance of all parties committing to dialogue and diplomacy” on implementing the US-Iran memorandum of understanding and safeguarding freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, per Xinhua (Aug 17). Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari separately reiterated Doha’s denial of detaining Iranian pilots, saying the country was “surprised by these misleading statements at this particular time.”

stories.headline: World Bank Report Ranks Qatar Among Economies Leading the AI Frontier
stories.body: The World Bank’s World Development Report 2026 placed Qatar alongside Singapore, Sweden and the UAE among economies advancing fastest on artificial intelligence, citing its “sustained investment in digital infrastructure” as it builds a knowledge-based economy, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 16). The report found AI could lift productivity in 18.7% of jobs in high-income countries versus 16.2% in developing economies, while automation risk from generative AI is estimated at 14.2% and 4.5% respectively.

doha_events.headline: Colorverse Experience Lights Up Katara Through Mid-September
doha_events.body: Katara Cultural Village is hosting Colorverse, a 45-minute immersive family attraction running July 15–Sept 15, with tickets from QR35. Visitors move through seven interactive zones to help “restore red, green and blue colours” to the fictional world of Colorama, with hands-on science activities, character meet-and-greets and workshops for ages four and up, per The Peninsula Qatar (Jun 6).

doha_events.headline: PAW Patrol: The Big Show Rescue Rolls Into Qatar Mall
doha_events.body: Nickelodeon’s PAW Patrol brings a live stage show, “The Big Show Rescue,” to Qatar Mall from Aug 20–29, with multiple free showtimes daily aimed at younger children and families, per Qatar Living’s events roundup (Aug 16).

doha_events.headline: Lusail Karting Sessions Return for the Week
doha_events.body: Lusail International Circuit is running public karting sessions Aug 19–22, 6pm–11pm, at QAR 125 for a roughly 12-minute session on its 900-metre track, per Qatar Living (Aug 16). The program, aimed at drivers 13 and up (minimum height 153cm), uses 270cc karts capable of 50–60 km/h, with bookings online-only and non-refundable.

doha_events.headline: Hala Summer Shopping Festival Raffle Hits Villaggio This Week
doha_events.body: Visit Qatar’s Hala Summer Shopping Festival runs across nine malls — including Villaggio, Place Vendôme, Doha Festival City and Mall of Qatar — through Aug 31, with Villaggio’s weekly raffle draw set for Aug 21 at 8:30pm. Shoppers spending a minimum QR200 get receipts stamped for raffle entry into prizes given out throughout the month, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 14).

doha_events.headline: Al Wakra Beach Cleanup Invites Volunteers on Aug 22
doha_events.body: The Ministry of Municipality’s ongoing coastal cleanup drive stops at Al Wakra Public Beach on Aug 22, with two free volunteer sessions from 6–9am and 3–5pm, per Qatar Living (Aug 16). It’s part of a wider series of beach and island cleanup campaigns the ministry has been running through the summer to promote environmental awareness.
